title: Man Killed by Tiger After Entering Enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park
excerpt: A man died on Saturday after entering the tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park near Doncaster, South Yorkshire Police said; the tiger was unharmed, the park was evacuated and will stay closed on Sunday.
body:
• A man died on Saturday after entering the tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park near Doncaster and being attacked by one of the big cats.
  • South Yorkshire Police were called at 1.35pm; despite the efforts of paramedics, the man was pronounced dead at the scene.
  • The tiger was unharmed, remained in the enclosure, and police say there is no wider risk to the public.
  • The park was evacuated and will remain closed on Sunday; police urged people not to share distressing footage of the attack circulating online.

A man has died after suffering serious injuries when he entered a tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park in northern England and was attacked, South Yorkshire Police said on Saturday. The man was pronounced dead at the scene despite the efforts of medical personnel.

"At 1.35pm today (Saturday 10 October) we received reports of a man entering a tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park," police said. "The tiger subsequently attacked the man, resulting in serious injury." The man's family has been informed and is being supported by specialist officers.

What happened

The attack took place at the park's "Land of the Tigers" exhibit near Doncaster. Video circulating on social media appears to show the man being mauled before he wagged his finger at the tiger in an apparent attempt to stop it. Police asked the public not to share the distressing footage.

https://x.com/Worldsource24/status/2108952125338185874

Witnesses said the man appeared to be alone. One visitor said he asked a total stranger to take his photograph with the tiger in the background before entering the enclosure, and told the local press she believed "he just wanted to play with the tiger." Another witness told The Sun she heard two noises like gunshots as staff responded. It remains unclear how the man got into the enclosure.

Two land ambulances, the Yorkshire Air Ambulance and a doctor attended the scene, according to the ambulance service. A black screen was erected around the enclosure after the incident, witnesses said.

Safety record under scrutiny

The death has renewed questions about how visitors gain access to restricted areas around big-cat enclosures. Wildlife parks in Britain operate under zoo licensing rules that require physical barriers capable of preventing unauthorised entry, and investigators will examine whether the enclosure's perimeter fencing and warning signage met those standards.

The park's response

Yorkshire Wildlife Park said a "serious incident" occurred at one of its tiger enclosures and that its emergency response procedures were immediately activated. The park was evacuated and will remain closed for the rest of Saturday and on Sunday.

The park, which opened in 2009, launched its Land of the Tigers attraction in 2011. It has said the safety and wellbeing of visitors, staff and animals remains its highest priority.

What's next

Police are investigating exactly how the man entered the enclosure. The tiger was uninjured and stayed in the enclosure after the attack, and authorities stressed there is no wider risk to the public. The park has said it will confirm when it can reopen.
